change_goal.text: walk at lunch with a coworker

scoreability.reason: 618 s (10 min 18 s) and a behavioral change goal reached.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thanks for coming in. What would you like us to focus on today?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: My doctor keeps telling me I need to move more. I sit at a desk all day, and by the time I get home I'm wiped out.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You're hearing it from your doctor, and at the same time your days leave you with not much left in the tank.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Exactly. I know walking would help. I used to walk all the time before this job.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Walking used to be a regular part of your life. What did you like about it back then?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It cleared my head. I'd come back from a walk and actually feel like myself again.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Walking was more than exercise for you. It was how you found your way back to yourself.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yeah. I miss that, honestly.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Part of you really wants that feeling back.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I do. I just don't see where it fits. My mornings are chaos with the kids.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You keep a demanding job and a busy family running, which takes real persistence. Where in your week might a walk fit, if anywhere?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Maybe lunch. We get an hour, and I usually just eat at my desk.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Lunch is a window that's already there.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It is. Even twenty minutes would be something.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Twenty minutes feels doable, and it sounds like it would really matter to you.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It would. I guess I worry what my coworkers would think if I'm the only one leaving.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Being the one who walks out feels a bit exposed, and it's completely your call. What might make it easier?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: If I asked Dana to come with me, it wouldn't feel so strange. She's always complaining about sitting too.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: A walking partner would turn it into something you do together instead of something you sneak off to do.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Right. I think I'll ask her tomorrow.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You've gone from not seeing where walking fits to a plan to ask Dana tomorrow.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I'll text myself a reminder at noon so I don't talk myself out of it.
